team2_assessment.rationale: Team 2 produced deep research across 4 areas with more specific metrics, concrete tool comparisons, and recent references (2025-2026 sources) than Team 1. Strengths include detailed library comparisons (PyPortfolioOpt vs Riskfolio-Lib vs skfolio), concrete code examples, specific benchmark results (FinRL Contest 2025), and comprehensive regulatory coverage (SR 11-7, EU AI Act, Bank of England SS1/23). Weaknesses include narrower scope (4 vs 8 areas), missing NLP/sentiment coverage, no alternative data section, and limited HFT coverage.

citation_quality.notes: 32 references across 4 topics, averaging 8 per topic. Good mix of academic papers, documentation, and industry reports. More recent sources than Team 1 (2025-2026 vs 2024-2025). Includes conference proceedings (NeurIPS 2025), official regulatory documents (EBA, CFA Institute), and primary library documentation.

coverage.notes: 42 unique techniques across 4 areas. Deep within each area but narrower overall scope. Missing: NLP/sentiment analysis, alternative data, HFT market microstructure, risk management. Compensated by deeper treatment of topics covered.

depth.notes: Substantially deeper than Team 1 on overlapping topics. ML Trading section includes specific model architectures (TRONformer, PrimoGPT/PrimoRL), contest results, and hybrid framework comparisons with adoption percentages. Portfolio section provides detailed library comparison matrix. Infrastructure section covers MLOps maturity levels. Regulatory section covers multiple jurisdictions.

specificity.notes: Strong quantitative specificity: precise Sharpe ratios (1.70, 1.57, 1.35), return figures (58.47%, 134.05%), MAE reductions (40-50%), market sizing ($1.58B MLOps, 35.5% CAGR), library versions (Riskfolio-Lib 7.2.1), and timing benchmarks (SHAP 0.3784s, LIME 0.1486s). 7 runnable code examples provided.

breadth.notes: Team 1 covered 8 areas with 57 techniques vs Team 2's 4 areas with 42 techniques. Team 1 has clear advantage in topic coverage.

depth.notes: Team 2 provides substantially deeper analysis per topic with specific benchmarks, library comparisons, code examples, and recent contest results.

citation_quality.notes: Team 2 has more recent sources (2025-2026) and zero detected citation errors vs Team 1's two incorrect arxiv IDs. Team 2 cites primary library documentation and official regulatory documents.

specificity.notes: Team 2 provides more precise quantitative metrics, runnable code examples, and concrete tool comparisons.

recency.notes: Team 2 includes 2025-2026 sources including FinRL Contest 2025, Riskfolio-Lib 7.2.1 (Feb 2026), EBA 2025 AI Act paper. Team 1's sources are mostly 2019-2023 with limited 2024+ content.

practitioner_utility.notes: Team 2 provides runnable code examples (7 vs Team 1's GitHub links), library comparison matrices, and MLOps maturity frameworks directly usable by practitioners.

head_to_head_comparison.summary: Team 2 wins narrowly (81 vs 80) by excelling in depth, citation quality, specificity, recency, and practitioner utility. Team 1's advantage is breadth (8 vs 4 areas), covering NLP/sentiment, alternative data, HFT, and risk management that Team 2 does not address. For a comprehensive reference, both teams' outputs should be combined: Team 1 for breadth and Team 2 for depth on overlapping topics.
